Descent stage · ALSEP · flag · retrieved parts of Surveyor 3

The precision landing — Conrad touched down within ~163 m of the uncrewed Surveyor 3 probe (1967). They retrieved pieces of it for return to Earth, showing spacecraft survive years on the Moon undamaged by radiation or micrometeorites. A proof-of-concept for future rendezvous missions.
First precision landing at a designated point — the prerequisite for any sample-return rendezvous architecture, including Mars.

Apollo 12 landed in Oceanus Procellarum on November 19, 1969 — a pinpoint landing within walking distance of the Surveyor 3 robotic lander that had touched down 2½ years earlier. Conrad and Bean spent 31h on the surface across two EVAs, carried back 34 kg of samples plus pieces of Surveyor 3 for analysis. Demonstrated that crewed Apollo could reach a specific target on the lunar surface.
Apollo 12 crew portrait — Pete Conrad (CDR), Dick Gordon (CMP), Al Bean (LMP).
November 14, 1969 — struck by lightning twice in the first minute
Saturn V SA-507 lifts off through a rain shower. Lightning hit the vehicle at T+36s and T+52s, knocking out fuel-cell power; SCE-to-AUX command saved the mission.
Conrad with the Surveyor 3 lander — Apollo 12 landed 163 m away, the first precision lunar landing.
ALSEP science station deployed — first long-duration lunar geophysical observatory.
Apollo 12 landing site panorama — Intrepid descent stage + ALSEP + Surveyor 3 within frame.
